question: 77th Independence Day was celebrated in which of the year?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2023**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's Independence Day is celebrated on **15th August** each year.
 
• The first Independence Day was celebrated on **15th August 1947**.
 
• The 77th Independence Day was celebrated in the year **2023**.
 
• Independence Day marks the end of British rule and the establishment of a free and independent Indian nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Independence Day:**

 
 
• It is a national holiday in India commemorating the nation's independence from the United Kingdom on 15 August 1947.
 
• The Independence movement was led by the Indian National Congress and many freedom fighters including Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Subhas Chandra Bose.
 
• On this day, the Prime Minister of India hoists the national flag at the Red Fort in Delhi and delivers an address to the nation.
 
• Independence Day is observed with flag-hoisting ceremonies, parades, cultural events, and the singing of patriotic songs across the country.
 
 
 
• **British Rule in India:**
 
 
• The British East India Company began its rule in India in 1757 after the Battle of Plassey and continued until 1858 when the British Crown took over following the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
• The period of British rule is known as the British Raj, which lasted until India gained independence in 1947.
 
• During British rule, India faced significant political, social, and economic changes, including the introduction of Western education, legal systems, and infrastructure development.
 
• The struggle for independence involved various movements and revolts against British policies and exploitation.
 
 
 
• **Freedom Fighters:**
 
 
• Several key figures played pivotal roles in India's struggle for independence, including Mahatma Gandhi, who advocated for non-violent resistance through his principles of Satyagraha and Ahimsa.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru, a prominent leader of the Indian National Congress, became the first Prime Minister of independent India.
 
• Subhas Chandra Bose led the Indian National Army (INA) against British forces during World War II.
 
• Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, and other revolutionaries contributed to the freedom struggle through armed resistance and sacrifices.
